extra.message: The user-supplied form field 'registration_code.code' is directly interpolated via f-string into a raw SQL string passed to text(). User input in validate_token() from routes/signup.py:16-17 creates an unparameterized SQL query, allowing attackers to bypass registration code validation or inject arbitrary SQL.

The 'search' URL parameter is directly interpolated via f-string into a raw SQL text fragment passed to SQLAlchemy's text(). In routes/account.py:33, the search query string becomes part of the WHERE clause without parameterization, allowing full SQL injection.

In routes/account.py:118, the 'before_request' handler deserializes user-controlled cookie data (base64-decoded from request.cookies['preferences']) using pickle.loads(). An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload in their cookie to achieve arbitrary code execution on the server during deserialization.

In utils/profile_image.py:7-8, urlopen() fetches a URL sourced from user input via form.url.data (routes/account.py:60) without any validation or whitelist. An attacker can provide URLs to internal services (e.g., http://localhost:5432, metadata endpoints like http://169.254.169.254), achieving server-side request forgery.

The get_personal_notes function at routes/account.py:43 accepts a user_id URL parameter and returns all notes for that user without verifying that current_user owns the requested user's account. Any authenticated user can enumerate and read another user's personal notes by manipulating the user_id path variable.

The delete_note function at routes/notes.py:41-49 has no ownership check. Any authenticated user can delete any note by supplying the note_id in the URL path. The code retrieves the note by ID via session.get(Note, note_id) and deletes it without verifying note.user_id == current_user.id.

The update_account function at routes/account.py:68-95 updates current_user.__dict__ with all form fields from AccountForm (forms/account_form.py:8 has an is_admin BooleanField). Since forms/account_form.py line 8 exposes 'is_admin' as a form field, any logged-in user can set is_admin=True via POST to /account, granting themselves admin privileges. The __dict__.update at line 81 applies all form data without restriction on which fields are safe for users to modify.
The Flask secret key is hardcoded as 'super secret key' in app.py:11. This allows any attacker to forge valid session cookies and hijack user sessions since they know the signing key.

The preferences cookie set in routes/account.py:105 lacks HttpOnly and Secure flags. Without HttpOnly, the cookie is accessible via JavaScript, enabling XSS-based cookie theft attacks. The insecure pickle data stored within the cookie could be read by malicious scripts.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in 'Session' Cookie without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: In utils/profile_image.py:13-14, mimetypes.guess_type(url) is used to determine the MIME type from a user-supplied URL without validation. An attacker can bypass this by encoding the filename in the URL (e.g., .png?victim.exe), allowing them to inject a malicious Content-Type header when the image blob is later served back to another user.

cwe: CWE-74: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output (Injection)

extra.message: The delete_note endpoint at routes/notes.py:39-52 has no CSRF token validation. The /login POST endpoint in routes/login.py:22 and the /signup POST in routes/signup.py:33 also lack CSRF protection (no hidden _csrf_token or equivalent). Any crafted form can force an authenticated user to delete notes, log in, or sign up from their browser.

The account modification endpoints (/account POST at routes/account.py:68 and /account/image POST at routes/account.py:51) lack CSRF token validation. An attacker can craft a page that auto-submits forms to modify user accounts or upload malicious profile images.
